task.title: Backgrounds
task.shortdesc: A background is a color, one or more images, or both, painted behind the content of a box. Use it to fill a box, to add a texture or a watermark, and to repeat a drawing on every page.

context.p: A background has up to two kinds of parts. The color is a single layer below everything else. The images are layers above the color, and you can have as many of them as you need. The first image of a list is the top layer.

info.p: The background-color property paints the whole background area with one color. It takes any CSS color, such as a name, a hexadecimal value or rgb(). The initial value is transparent.
The background of the root element fills the page area, which is the part of the page inside the page margins. To paint the page margins too, set a background in an @page rule.

The background-image property takes a list of images separated by commas. An image can be a file, written as url(), or a gradient such as linear-gradient(), radial-gradient(), conic-gradient() and their repeating forms. The value none is a layer without an image, and it is the initial value.
The watermark is above the gradient, and the background color is below both. A relative url() is found from the location of the stylesheet.
An image is placed in the positioning area of the box. The background-origin property chooses it: padding-box, which is the initial value, border-box or content-box.

The background-position property moves the image inside that area. A value can be a keyword (left, center, right, top and bottom), a length or a percentage. With one value, the second is center. With two values, the first is the horizontal position and the second is the vertical one. A keyword followed by a length is an offset from that side. The initial value is 0% 0%, the top left corner.
A percentage aligns the same point of the image and of the area. 50% centers the image and 100% puts its right edge on the right edge of the area.

The properties background-position-x and background-position-y set one axis. background-position-inline and background-position-block set an axis by the direction of the text, with start and end instead of the side keywords.
The background-size property sets the size of an image. The initial value, auto, is the size of the image. These are the other values:

ul.li: A length or a percentage of the positioning area sets the width. A second value sets the height. If you give only one, the height is auto, and CSSMedia keeps the proportions of the image.
cover makes the image as small as possible so that it covers the whole area. A part of the image can be left out.
contain makes the image as large as possible so that all of it fits in the area. A part of the area can stay empty.

info.p: An image repeats until it fills the area. The background-repeat property sets how, with one value for both axes, or two values for the horizontal and the vertical axis:

ul.li: repeat is the initial value. It repeats the image and cuts the last copy at the edge.
space draws as many whole copies as fit and spreads them with equal space between them.
round draws as many whole copies as fit, and resizes them so that they fill the area exactly.

image.alt: Four boxes filled with a square tile that has a white dot. With repeat, the last copies are cut at the edge. With no-repeat, there is one tile. With space, there are whole tiles with gaps between them. With round, whole tiles are stretched to fill the box.

info.p: The values repeat-x and repeat-y repeat on one axis only, and repeat-inline and repeat-block do it by the direction of the text. The properties background-repeat-x, background-repeat-y, background-repeat-inline and background-repeat-block set one axis.

step.cmd: Attach an image to the page

info.p: The background-attachment property is scroll by default, which attaches the image to its box. With fixed, the image is attached to the page, so it is placed the same way on every page where the box has a background. A value of local works as scroll, because a page does not scroll.
The background-clip property chooses the area where the background is painted:

ul.li: border-box is the initial value. The background goes under the border.
padding-box stops it at the inner edge of the border.
content-box paints only the content area.
border-area paints only under the border.
text paints only inside the shapes of the letters of the box, which makes text that is filled with an image or a gradient. You can combine border-area and text.

fig.title: The areas of background-origin and background-clip

image.alt: Three boxes with a border, padding and content. The background is painted under the border for border-box, up to the border for padding-box, and in the content area only for content-box.

info.p: The background-blend-mode property sets how each image layer mixes with the layers below it and with the color. The modes are normal, which is the initial value, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, color-dodge, color-burn, hard-light, soft-light, difference, exclusion, hue, saturation, color and luminosity. Give one mode for each layer, separated by commas. When the list is shorter than the list of images, it repeats.

The background property sets all the background properties in one declaration. Separate the layers with commas, and put the color in the last layer. In a layer, write a position, then a slash and a size, and in any order the image, the repeat style, the attachment and one or two boxes. One box sets the origin and the clip. Two boxes set the origin first and the clip second. A property that you leave out goes back to its initial value, background-blend-mode included.
The background-tbd property is like background, but it takes no color and leaves the color as it is.
